sources.note: Discusses HTL(E) and HTL(K) historically; gives a comparative consonant table for Motu/Toaripi/Orokolo/Koriki (p. 73). No statement about stress in HTL(K) (only a quoted Toaripi>Orokolo sound rule mentioning a stressed vowel, p. 88, irrelevant).

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 1979. Simplified Koriki: a second trade language used by the Motu in the Gulf of Papua. Kivung 12(1): 3-73.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only primary description of HTL(K). Sec. 2.0 (pp. 7-8) sketches the phonology of Koriki proper (the lexifier): 7 consonants, 5 vowels, open syllables, and 'Stress is important.' -- no position given. Sec. 3.21.1 'Phonology' of Moi Higo's Simplified Koriki (p. 14) treats only segmental variation (u~o, n~r, m~v, dropped glottal stop); nothing on stress. Appendix 6 wordlist marks length but not stress. Silent on stress placement in the pidgin.
